subject: POC / Trial planning: workload profile & success criteria - AcmeHealth

Subject: POC / Trial planning: workload profile & success criteria - AcmeHealth

Hi Sasha —

Great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps for the POC/trial: 

Key objectives (from today):
- Validate latency under production-like traffic for the clinical triage model (goal: 95th pct latency < 300ms for single-turn inference).
- Measure token-cost and unit economics for our expected workload patterns.
- Verify data controls / retention settings meet AcmeHealth compliance needs.

POC scope (proposed):
- 2-week trial using Redwood Dedicated with a snapshot of your clinical triage model (or a compatible open architecture we discussed).
- Simulated traffic mirroring your production RPS and burst patterns (see initial ask below).
- Success criteria: latency SLO, throughput (RPS), accuracy delta < 2% vs current baseline, and cost per 1M tokens.

Request: can you confirm the workload profile so we can size the Dedicated pool and finalize the SOW? Specifically we need:
- Steady-state RPS and expected peak bursts (RPS and duration)
- Typical and 95th percentile token lengths per request (input + output)
- Concurrency targets (simultaneous requests)
- Any hard latency SLOs for specific routes

I've attached a short workload_profile_template.xlsx to make this quick to fill out. I've also attached a one-page SOW draft for review.

Tentative timeline:
- Receive workload profile by Thu 24 Mar
- Finalize SOW and schedule Dedicated hardware by Mon 28 Mar
- POC start: Mon 04 Apr (2 weeks)

Ownership: Ben (sales) + Marissa (solutions engineer) from our side. We'll loop in infra/ops if we need a faster hardware ramp.

Next steps: please confirm or propose changes to success criteria and drop the workload numbers in the template.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0142

From: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@acmehealth.com>

Date: 2027-03-22T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC / Trial planning: workload profile & success criteria - AcmeHealth

Ben — thanks for the clear recap and the template. Forwarding to Amir and our infra folks, but answering the workload questions below (high level) so you can start sizing: 

Workload (high level):
- Steady-state RPS: 45 req/s across the cluster (this is end-user requests after our edge routing).
- Peak bursts: up to 220 req/s sustained for spikes of 90–180s (typically triggered by morning intake windows).
- Typical token length: 120 tokens input, 80 tokens output (200 tokens total median).
- 95th percentile token length: 560 tokens total (long reports).
- Concurrency: we see ~40 concurrent long-running requests at 95th percentile.
- Hard SLO: for triage endpoint, 95th pct latency target <= 350ms; average should be < 150ms.

Also: data residency note — all PHI must stay within our US region and log retention needs to be configurable (30–90 days).

I'll have Amir share more precise traces and an anonymized sample payloads (we'll strip PHI) by end of day tomorrow.

Thanks,
Sasha
Sasha Patel
Dir. Product Ops, AcmeHealth
Sasha.Patel@acmehealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-03-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC / Trial planning: workload profile & success criteria - AcmeHealth

Sasha — appreciate the quick numbers, this is exactly what we need. A few follow-ups/questions so the sizing is accurate: 

1) For the 220 req/s bursts: are those mostly short requests (<= 200 tokens) or mixed with the long-report 95th-percentile requests?
2) You mentioned concurrency ~40 for long requests — is that per region or global? We should treat that as simultaneous model invocations for KV cache sizing.
3) Regarding retention: we can make retention configurable; two things to confirm: do you require logs to be forwarded to your SIEM, or is local retention sufficient for the trial?

We'll draft a recommended Dedicated pool config (GPU type + replicas), expected cost estimate for the 2-week run, and a test harness that will replay the traces you share. Marissa — can you provision an initial test config and draft the SLO measurement plan?

Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC / Trial planning: workload profile & success criteria - AcmeHealth

Looping in our solutions infra lead, Dylan, for sizing. Dylan — initial plan:
- Start with 4x A10G-ish machines (or equivalent) with continuous batching and prefix caching enabled.
- KV cache sized for 40 concurrent long-running requests; that will keep the KV footprint in GPU memory small for typical dialogues.
- We'll run a replay harness that mixes short and long requests to simulate the 220 RPS bursts.
- For retention: default trial config keeps logs in-region for 30 days; we can configure a forward to their SIEM if they provide an endpoint.

I will prepare:
- A test plan (SLO measurement script, datasets to use)
- Expected cost estimate for the 2-week Dedicated run
- A list of data controls to include in the SOW (retention, KMS, audit logs)

Ben — I'll share the config and cost estimate by EOD Mon 28 Mar.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — good signal. Next steps and owners: 

1) Acme to share anonymized traces & sample payloads (Amir) — target: 2027-03-23 EOD (I see the Drive link; will confirm access).
2) Redwood to deliver SOW + cost estimate + Dedicated config (Ben / Marissa) — target: 2027-03-28 EOD.

Success criteria (confirmed):
- 95th pct latency for triage endpoint <= 350ms during steady and spike windows.
- Throughput: support sustained 45 RPS and tolerate 220 RPS bursts as described with acceptable degradation.
- Accuracy: model outputs within 2% accuracy delta vs baseline (customer to supply baseline eval set).
- Data controls: retention configurable to 30 days, with optional SIEM forward.

Attachments: POC_SOW_draft.pdf (updated stub) and workload_profile_template.xlsx (filled with Acme high-level numbers).
